skill.name: configuring-dapr-pubsub
skill.description: Configures Dapr pub/sub components, subscriptions, publishers, and Kubernetes sidecars for event-driven services using Kafka or Redis.
skill.summary: Configure Dapr pub/sub messaging patterns for Kafka or Redis microservices.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: I adjudicated all 51 static findings as false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline formatting, local Dapr sidecar URLs, and validation text. I found one semantic issue: production-labeled Kafka guidance uses authType none and the quick start disables TLS, which may encourage insecure broker deployments.

remediation.issue: Kafka examples include unauthenticated or TLS-disabled settings in quick start and production-labeled sections.
remediation.suggestion: Mark these settings as development-only and make SASL or TLS with Kubernetes secrets the production default.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Kafka Defaults in Production Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The quick start uses authType none and disables TLS, and the section titled Kafka Production also sets authType none. This can guide users toward unauthenticated or unencrypted broker deployments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited YAML directly sets authType to none and disableTls to true, including under a production-labeled Kafka section. The skill later shows SASL, but the production label makes the insecure default credible.

content.value_statement: Event-driven services need consistent pub/sub setup across local and Kubernetes environments. This skill provides Dapr component, subscription, publishing, and troubleshooting patterns for Kafka or Redis.
actual_capabilities: Generates Dapr pub/sub component YAML for Kafka and Redis.
Shows declarative and programmatic subscription patterns.
Provides FastAPI publishing and handler examples through a Dapr sidecar.
Demonstrates Kubernetes Dapr sidecar annotations and component scoping.
Includes local Dapr CLI and Docker Compose development patterns.
Provides troubleshooting checks for metadata, logs, topics, and routes.
limitations: Does not replace Dapr or broker documentation for version-specific settings.
Does not provision Kafka, Redis, or Kubernetes clusters.
Uses illustrative service names and ports that require environment changes.
Some examples need stronger production security settings before deployment.

use_cases.title: Standardize Dapr messaging components
use_cases.description: Create consistent Kafka or Redis pub/sub component definitions for multiple services and namespaces.

use_cases.title: Wire FastAPI event flows
use_cases.description: Add Dapr subscription endpoints, publish events, and handle CloudEvent payloads in Python services.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot delivery failures
use_cases.description: Check sidecar logs, component registration, topics, routes, and consumer group behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic pub/sub component
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Dapr pub/sub component for Redis for local development. Include required metadata and explain what I must change.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Kafka subscription
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Dapr declarative subscription for my service. Use Kafka pub/sub, topic order-created, route /dapr/order-created, and a narrow scope.

prompt_templates.title: Wire publisher and handler services
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me connect two FastAPI services with Dapr pub/sub. Show the publisher flow, subscriber route, event fields, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review production readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Dapr pub/sub design for production. Check authentication, TLS, secrets, retries, component scopes, consumer groups, and Kubernetes sidecars.

output_examples.input: I need Kafka-backed Dapr pub/sub for three agent services in Kubernetes.
output_examples.output: A scoped component plan, subscription topics for each service, sidecar annotations, and validation checks for metadata and logs.

output_examples.input: My local subscriber is not receiving events from a Dapr publisher.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting sequence covering sidecar startup, component registration, topic names, route paths, and subscriber logs.

output_examples.input: I want to move from Redis development pub/sub to Kafka production pub/sub.
output_examples.output: A migration checklist covering broker settings, authentication, secrets, consumer groups, scopes, and deployment differences.

best_practices: Keep component scopes narrow so only intended services can use each pub/sub component.
Store broker credentials in Kubernetes secrets and prefer TLS or SASL for production brokers.
Test publisher and subscriber paths with the Dapr sidecar before deploying many replicas.
anti_patterns: Treating development settings such as disabled TLS as production defaults.
Publishing directly to Kafka when the service contract requires Dapr pub/sub.
Reusing one consumer group across unrelated apps without checking delivery semantics.

faq.question: Does this skill create Kafka or Redis clusters?
faq.answer: No. It helps configure Dapr pub/sub components that connect to existing Kafka or Redis infrastructure.

faq.question: Can I use it with Kubernetes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes component YAML, subscriptions, Dapr sidecar annotations, scopes, and deployment patterns.

faq.question: Does it support CloudEvents?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how handlers read CloudEvent data and how publishers can include CloudEvent metadata.

faq.question: Is Redis suitable for production pub/sub?
faq.answer: Redis can work for simple cases, but production needs depend on durability, ordering, scale, and operational requirements.

faq.question: Does the skill execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. Commands are documentation examples for users to run in their own Dapr and Kubernetes environments.

faq.question: What should I review before production?
faq.answer: Review authentication, TLS, secrets, component scopes, retry behavior, consumer groups, topic names, and sidecar health.
